clue.text: I'd meet MP in cocktail bar

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these words are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suggests meeting a Member of Parliament in a cocktail bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail bar' reads as one place, but 'cocktail' is the anagram signal and 'bar' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar in the sense of an obstacle or hindrance is a synonym.

clue.text: This month in Westminster

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the word Westminster

explanation.surface: Something happening this month at the seat of the British Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: INST is short for 'instant', an old business-letter abbreviation meaning of the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: An old commercial abbreviation of the Latin instante mense, of the present month.

clue.text: Show displeasure when nothing is in place

indicators.note: is in says the zero goes inside the word for place

parts.note: to put is to place
O looks like the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sulks when something is missing from where it belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing the lips out sulkily is a facial sign of annoyance.

clue.text: Torrid disposition of little Dickensian heroine

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: The fiery temperament of a small heroine from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' is part of the definition: Little Dorrit is the Dickens novel named after its heroine Amy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy, the title character of the novel Little Dorrit, is a Dickens heroine.

clue.text: Offices used by union negotiators?

parts.note: union suggests trade unions bargaining, but here it is wedlock: agencies arranging matches

explanation.surface: Rooms where trade-union officials bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchmaking agencies help people negotiate a union in wedlock.

clue.text: Mug one may put one's teeth into?

definitions.meaning: a mug is a fool or simpleton, also slang for head

definitions.text: one may put one's teeth into?
definitions.meaning: pasta such as spaghetti strands is bitten into

explanation.surface: A drinking cup you might bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is slang for a fool or head, and also a strip of pasta eaten.

clue.text: A boundary gives us the lead

definitions.meaning: an advantage, as in having the upper hand over rivals

explanation.surface: Hitting a boundary in cricket puts the team ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Edge is both a border and an advantage over competitors.

clue.text: Upset there is, and dismay

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is upset, and dismayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as an emotion matching 'dismay', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to discourage them, a synonym.

clue.text: Choose to speak for the voters

parts.note: to elect is to choose
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Picking someone to be the voters' spokesperson.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of all people entitled to vote is a collective synonym.

clue.text: Old fashioned origin of a mathematical function

parts.note: square is slang for conventional, out of date
a root is a source or origin

explanation.surface: The quaint beginnings of a maths operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the number that multiplied by itself gives a value is a standard maths operation.

clue.text: Land in the water

parts.note: a piece of ground surrounded by sea or lake

explanation.surface: Ground surrounded by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a stretch of ground with water all round it.

clue.text: They have a back-breaking job keeping down vermin

definitions.text: They have a back-breaking job keeping down vermin

parts.words: They have a back-breaking job keeping down vermin
parts.note: back-breaking sounds like hard toil but literally the spring snaps the rodent's spine

explanation.surface: Pest controllers with an exhausting job.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring traps kill rodents by snapping down on their backs.

clue.text: Skills shown by artiste, but presented badly

indicators.note: badly presented means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer's talents shown off poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualities or talents someone has are a synonym.

clue.text: Not having been given a good hiding?

definitions.text: Not having been given a good hiding?

parts.words: Not having been given a good hiding?
parts.note: a good hiding sounds like a thrashing, but here it means a place to stay concealed

explanation.surface: A child spared a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not well concealed can be seen.

clue.text: Grape-producer holds a label to mark its year

indicators.note: holds says the plant word wraps round the label word

parts.note: grapes grow on a vine
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A vineyard puts a tag on the bottle to show when it was made.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's vintage is the year its grapes were harvested.

clue.text: Nurse in bizarre sex case holds out

indicators.note: in says the caring word goes inside the scrambled letters
bizarre means weird, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A carer involved in an odd sexual scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is the outer shell: the scrambled letters EXS, made by 'bizarre', surround the caring word, as 'in' signals; 'holds out' means stretches forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend is to stretch or offer out, a synonym.

clue.text: Not in appropriate costume

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: Someone not wearing suitable clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of clothes worn together is a synonym.

clue.text: Former forward, and a very good one too

parts.note: ex means former
pert means cheeky, forward

explanation.surface: An ex-striker who was also highly skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly skilled person is a specialist or master.

clue.text: He picks up the litter

parts.note: litter sounds like rubbish, but it is a stretcher for carrying the wounded

explanation.surface: A street cleaner collecting rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is a stretcher, and this person carries casualties on one.

clue.text: Island where to shoot duck?

parts.note: to bag game is to shoot it
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O

explanation.surface: Asking where to go hunting wildfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, partner of Trinidad.

clue.text: End of the beef soup?

parts.note: end suggests the last of a meal, but it is the rear end of a cow, made into broth

explanation.surface: The last of the meaty broth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's tail, the animal's rear end, is made into a well-known soup.

clue.text: Notice a gap coming

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: An announcement that a vacancy is on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival or coming, as in the advent of spring, is a synonym.

clue.text: Usual place for a wake

parts.note: a wake sounds like a funeral gathering, but it is the trail of water behind a ship

explanation.surface: Where a funeral party is usually held.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's trail of disturbed water lies behind it, at the back.

clue.text: Not stopping to communicate

definitions.meaning: a non-stop fast train or service

explanation.surface: Talking without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: Express means a fast non-stop train, and also to convey a thought.

clue.text: Performs with wild cats

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A circus act with untamed big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on stage is to perform.

clue.text: Earl created king

indicators.note: created means made anew, so the letters are formed into another order

explanation.surface: A nobleman elevated to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is the Shakespeare monarch.

clue.text: Raise the stake for a fiery mount

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: the ante is the stake put in at poker

explanation.surface: A poker player upping the bet on a volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' looks like a poker move to match 'stake', but it signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a Sicilian volcano, a mountain that erupts fire.

clue.text: "Get mean, man!" ordered the bosses

indicators.note: ordered means put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bosses commanding a worker to be tougher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like the bosses giving a command, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who run a company are collectively its managers.

clue.text: Corporation band

parts.note: corporation suggests a municipal brass band, but it is a jokey word for a paunch, and the band goes round it

explanation.surface: A town council's brass band.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a strip of cloth worn round the waist, where a big belly sits.

clue.text: Boy goes to an unusually arid place in Egypt

parts.note: Alex is a boy's name

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lad travels to a strangely dry spot in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandria is the Egyptian port city founded by Alexander the Great.
